name: Twenty
one_liner: Twenty is an open-source, extensible CRM (cloud or self-hosted) with REST and GraphQL APIs, workflows, AI agents, and an apps framework for building custom CRMs and internal tools.

auth.note: OAuth2 authorization code + PKCE and client credentials against the API; API keys also documented

access.note: Free 30-day trial with no credit card; self-hosting free; API included on all plans
Dynamic client registration, no manual vendor review

api_surface.note: Core and Metadata APIs in REST and GraphQL, generated per workspace schema

mcp.note: Official MCP server on the workspace URL, OAuth or API key

verdict.note: REST & GraphQL API, Webhooks and MCP server available on all plans, with rate limits

notes: API keys are generated in Settings; the fetched pages do not show their exact format. Rate limits are 50/min on Pro and 100/min on Organization. Webhooks exist. The OAuth docs state the Core and Metadata APIs accept OAuth tokens. Admin requirements for installs are not shown.

name: Twilio
one_liner: Twilio is a cloud communications platform with APIs for SMS, voice, WhatsApp, email, video, phone verification and customer data, plus conversation products built for AI agents.

auth.note: Official SDK samples authenticate with Account SID and Auth Token.
Help article title shows API key and secret authentication; page body did not render.

access.note: Free trial with no credit card, then pay as you go.
Sign up for a free account and use the SDKs.

mcp.note: Official hosted MCP server at mcp.twilio.com/docs, Public Beta, read-only docs search.

verdict.note: Documented SDKs and credentials available after self-serve signup.

notes: The Account SID and Auth Token scheme is inferred from SDK samples, which use HTTP basic auth. API key/secret is seen only in a help article title. No third-party API OAuth was documented. The official MCP is read-only docs search (no auth, Public Beta); OAuth execution tools are only planned. Community SendGrid MCP tutorial exists.

name: Plain
one_liner: Plain is a customer support platform for B2B teams that unifies Slack, email and chat threads with customer context and AI agents, exposing a full GraphQL API, an MCP server and an option to bring your own agents.

auth.note: Machine user API keys sent as a Bearer header
OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE for third-party apps calling the API

access.note: 7-day free trial with no credit card; self-serve plans
Developer platform (API, webhooks, MCP) is listed across the plans

api_surface.note: The GraphQL API is the same one the UI uses, so there are no limitations

mcp.note: Official MCP server at mcp.plain.com with about 400 tools

verdict.note: Self-serve API key creation in Settings

notes: The MCP server uses OAuth only (no API keys); that is separate from the API auth listed here. The OAuth app is workspace-specific. The "External Agents" (bring your own agent) feature is listed under the Frontier plan on one help page. Whether admin rights are needed to create machine users or OAuth apps is not shown.

name: GoHighLevel
one_liner: GoHighLevel (HighLevel) is an all-in-one CRM, marketing automation and agency platform with a REST API, OAuth marketplace apps, webhooks and an official MCP server.

auth.note: Quick start lists OAuth 2.0 or Private Integration Token with Bearer header

access.note: 14-day free trial; API access is a plan feature (basic API access on Unlimited)
Choose Marketplace app or Private integration

api_surface.note: REST API covering contacts, conversations, calendars, opportunities, payments, 50+ webhook events

mcp.note: Official HighLevel MCP Server docs with 700+ actions

verdict.note: Documented REST API with OAuth and private tokens, self-serve signup

notes: Pricing page indicates API access varies by plan (Unlimited has basic API access), so a paid plan or trial may be needed. Public marketplace app distribution requires app review (not confirmed in pages). MCP uses OAuth sign-in. Admin requirement for installs not shown.

name: Sherlock
one_liner: Sherlock is an open-source Python command-line tool that checks a username across 400+ social networks and saves the accounts it finds to local files.

auth.note: Local CLI install and usage with no credentials or hosted API.

access.note: MIT-licensed, installable via pipx, Docker or dnf.

api_surface.note: CLI only, with options for output formats, proxy, site filter and timeout.

mcp.note: Third-party FastMCP server that wraps the Sherlock CLI. No official MCP found in the Sherlock repo README.

verdict.note: A wrappable local CLI counts as buildable_now.

notes: The product is a local CLI with no hosted API. The Burnsedia MCP is community-made. Pages about other products named Sherlock (a lock library, Synopsys, CloudFerro, Covertlabs) were ignored. The tool probes third-party sites, so their terms and rate limits may apply.

name: Linear
one_liner: Linear is an issue tracking and project management tool for software teams, with a GraphQL API, webhooks, a TypeScript SDK, an agent platform and an official hosted MCP server.

auth.note: OAuth2 authorization code, PKCE and client credentials against the Linear API
Mentions Linear API key / bearer token auth

access.note: Free plan includes API and webhook access

api_surface.note: GraphQL API, webhooks, attachments, customers, TypeScript SDK, agent docs

mcp.note: Official remote MCP server at mcp.linear.app/mcp

verdict.note: API access included on all plans, including Free

notes: API keys are only evidenced via the MCP page ("Linear API key"); the personal API key docs were not fetched. Webhooks and a TypeScript SDK exist. Admin requirement for installing OAuth apps in a workspace is not shown in the fetched pages.

name: Datadog
one_liner: Datadog is a cloud observability and security platform for monitoring infrastructure, applications, logs and more, exposed through a broad HTTP REST API, official client libraries and an official MCP server.

auth.note: API key and application key headers

access.note: Keys managed by the customer in their own account settings
Pricing page mentions a free trial

api_surface.note: HTTP REST API with official client libraries

verdict.note: Documented REST API with key-based auth

notes: API auth is the API key plus an application key for read endpoints. The MCP server uses OAuth 2.0 by default (API/app key headers as fallback); that OAuth is MCP-only, so it is not in auth_methods. Account signup and key creation were not directly shown; the free trial is inferred from a pricing page snippet.

name: Amazon Selling Partner
one_liner: Amazon's REST-based Selling Partner API (SP-API) lets sellers and vendors programmatically access orders, listings, inventory, shipments, payments and reports, and build apps for the Selling Partner Appstore.

auth.note: OAuth 2.0 via LWA for public apps; self-authorization for private apps

access.note: Professional account and developer profile evaluated by Amazon
Public developers must list in the Appstore

api_surface.note: REST-based SP-API docs with many API families

mcp.note: SP-API docs index lists no MCP server

verdict.note: Developer profile review gates API access

notes: Private apps use self-authorization via Seller Central. Restricted Data Tokens are needed for PII operations. Amazon Ads MCP and AWS Partner Central MCP pages are different products, not SP-API. Selling-partner admin requirement for authorizing a public app was not shown.

name: Paygent Connect
one_liner: Paygent Connect is described as an NMI-powered payment gateway product, but none of the fetched pages document it, so its function is not confirmed.

auth.note: Different product (AI agent spend/plan gating); not evidence for Paygent Connect.

access.note: Different Paygent product (API payments alternative to Stripe/PayPal); no NMI-powered Paygent Connect signup found.

api_surface.note: AI usage billing product, not the NMI-powered gateway.

mcp.note: No MCP server found; page belongs to a different Paygent product.

verdict.note: Cronos AI payment orchestration; unrelated to the NMI-powered Paygent Connect.

notes: Official Paygent Connect (NMI-powered) product not identified. Fetched pages cover other Paygent-named products (paygent.to AI spend gating, withpaygent.com AI billing, gopaygent.com, paygent.uk Cronos). Auth undocumented in fetched pages. Access value is a placeholder.

name: Devin
one_liner: Devin is an autonomous AI software engineer (by Cognition) that writes, runs and tests code, with a REST API, CLI, desktop app and an official MCP server.

auth.note: Service user API keys and PATs, cog_ bearer tokens in Authorization header

access.note: Free, Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise plans; Devin API listed in plan comparison
Self-provisioned service users in Settings > Devin API

api_surface.note: v3 Organization and Enterprise REST APIs

mcp.note: Official Devin MCP server at https://mcp.devin.ai/mcp

notes: Exact plan tier needed for API access isn't shown in the fetched pricing text (Devin API row is listed without per-plan detail). Enterprise API is enterprise-only. Legacy v1/v2 keys are deprecated. MCP server supports the same API keys; the CLI MCP client uses OAuth only for third-party servers.
